einzeiler: Three Democratic mayors discuss local governance, polarization and urban revitalization.
kurzfassung: Kara Swisher talks with the Democratic mayors of Denver, Kansas City and New Orleans about governing amid intense political polarization. The discussion covers practical approaches to local challenges like housing, homelessness, public safety and immigration. They also touch on national politics, party messaging and upcoming elections.
stichpunkte: Mayors face intense political polarization and friction with state governments in conservative-leaning states.
Denver experienced significant drops in homicide and homelessness rates while managing a large influx of migrants.
New Orleans recently completed an eight-month National Guard deployment and implemented crime prevention investments.
Kansas City and Denver are leveraging major events like the FIFA World Cup and large infrastructure projects for economic development.
Data centers present a growing political challenge for cities due to heavy water and electricity demands.
Housing trust funds and rapid transitional housing strategies are being used to combat homelessness and affordability issues.
Immigration enforcement and federal policies have created tensions, with mayors defending pro-immigrant city policies.
Gerrymandering and voting restrictions threaten democratic participation, prompting local leaders to prepare for election protection.

clips.hook: Denver saw massive drops in crime and homelessness during a migrant surge
clips.text: Despite receiving a high per capita number of migrants and facing negative narratives, Denver experienced record declines in both homicide and homelessness rates.

clips.hook: A massive 30 billion dollar investment drives Denver's revitalization
clips.text: A substantial multibillion-dollar funding initiative aims to generate numerous new employment opportunities and economic growth.

clips.hook: Denver achieved a massive reduction in unsheltered homelessness
clips.text: City leadership reports a substantial percentage decrease in street homelessness since taking office through targeted interventions.

clips.hook: Protecting the city mattered more than political consequences
clips.text: Local leadership prioritized taking immediate public action to defend the community over calculating political fallout or potential repercussions.

clips.hook: Washington politics drives citizens to deep frustration
clips.text: National politics is widely perceived as constant dysfunction, chaos, and disaster rather than delivering constructive solutions for citizens.

beschreibung:
Ahead of the midterms and what’s shaping up to be an intense political season, Kara speaks with the Democratic mayors of three cities dealing with some of the biggest issues facing the nation including affordability, housing, gerrymandering and immigration.

Mike Johnston is the first-term Mayor of Denver, Colorado. A former teacher, school principal and Colorado state senator, Mike is also a vice president of the Democratic Mayors Association.

Quinton Lucas is the Mayor of Kansas City, Missouri, currently in his second term. He’s also the youngest person elected to the role since 1855. An attorney and former city councilman, Quinton is the President of the Democratic Mayors Association.

Helena Moreno is the Mayor of New Orleans. She began her first term in office this year. Previously she served on the city council and as a Louisiana state legislator. Before getting into politics, she worked as a journalist. She’s the first Latina mayor of New Orleans and the city’s second woman mayor.
